# Rust UI

> Accessible, animated, shadcn-style components for Dioxus 0.7 (web and the desktop webview; native Blitz is a preview). Use them as source copied into your app (`rust-ui add <name>` or `dx components add`) or as the `rust-ui-kit` crate from git.

Rules for writing app code with this kit:

- Dioxus is pinned to `0.7.x`. Write Dioxus 0.7 code (`#[component]`, `rsx!`, signals); don't use 0.6 or 0.8 APIs.
- Load the theme once near the root: `ui::ThemeStyles {}` with the crate, or `document::Stylesheet { href: asset!("/assets/theme.css") }` after `rust-ui init`. Without it components are unstyled.
- Import components from `ui::prelude::*` with the crate, or `crate::components::<name>::*` after copying. Icons come from `ui::icons` by path (`ui::icons::Check`), hooks from `ui::hooks`, animation from `ui::motion`.
- Restyle with `class` (it adds to the kit's class) and the theme's CSS custom properties (`--primary-color`, `--accent-color`, `--radius`, ...). Don't hard-code colours, and don't change a component's markup: ARIA roles, focus and keys come from `dioxus-primitives`.
- Light and dark mode: `data-theme="light"` or `"dark"` on `<html>`; accent presets: `data-accent="blue|green|violet|rose|orange"`.
- Every interactive component works with the keyboard and every animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; keep it that way in your own code.
- Don't add JavaScript (`document::eval`) to get behaviour the kit already has. Ctrl+K and other shortcuts go through `ui::hooks::use_hotkey`.
- Each component page below has its props (the Rust signatures) and a working example. Prefer the example's patterns over guessing prop names.

Paths are relative to the repository root. `rust-ui docs <name>` prints a component page.

## Docs

- [Installing components](docs/INSTALL.md): copy the source with `rust-ui` or `dx`, or depend on the crate from git
- [Theming](docs/THEMING.md): light and dark mode, accent presets, a brand colour, radius
- [Icons](docs/ICONS.md): the Lucide set and when an icon needs a label
- [Stability](docs/STABILITY.md): which items are stable, experimental or internal
- [Everything](llms-full.txt): this index plus every component page in one file

## Components

- [Accordion](llms/accordion.md): The accordion component is used to display collapsible content panels for presenting information in a limited amount of space
- [Alert](llms/alert.md): A message that interrupts: it is announced as soon as it appears
- [Alert dialog](llms/alert_dialog.md): The AlertDialog primitive provides an accessible, composable modal dialog for critical user confirmations (such as destructive actions)
- [Aspect ratio](llms/aspect_ratio.md): The AspectRatio component is used to maintain a specific aspect ratio for its children
- [Avatar](llms/avatar.md): The Avatar components display a user's profile picture or fallback initials
- [Badge](llms/badge.md): The Badge is a component designed to display small, distinct labels that help highlight important content or status indicators
- [BottomNav](llms/bottom_nav.md): A mobile-style tab bar of links or buttons
- [Breadcrumb](llms/breadcrumb.md): A trail of links to the current page
- [Button](llms/button.md): The button element is used to trigger actions or events in a user interface
- [ButtonGroup](llms/button_group.md): Joins buttons or inputs into a segmented control, horizontal or vertical
- [Calendar](llms/calendar.md): The Calendar component is used to display a calendar interface, allowing users to select dates
- [Callout](llms/callout.md): An inline note (info, success, warning) for docs and forms
- [Card](llms/card.md): The card component is a flexible container for grouping related content and actions
- [Carousel](llms/carousel.md): A horizontally scrolling row of slides with scroll snapping and Previous/Next buttons
- [Chart](llms/chart.md): `BarChart` and `LineChart` drawn as SVG from a list of `ChartDatum`
- [Checkbox](llms/checkbox.md): The Checkbox component is used to create an accessible checkbox input
- [Chips](llms/chips.md): A row of on/off chips for filters and multi-choice tags
- [Collapsible](llms/collapsible.md): The `Collapsible` component allows users to create expandable sections that can be toggled open or closed
- [Color picker](llms/color_picker.md): Color picker used when the user needs to make a customized color selection
- [Combobox](llms/combobox.md): The Combobox component is an autocomplete input with a filterable popup list
- [Command](llms/command.md): A command palette: a search box over a filtered list, inside a dialog
- [Context menu](llms/context_menu.md): The context menu component can be used to define a context menu that is displayed when the user right-clicks on an element
- [DataTable](llms/data_table.md): A table with sorting, a filter box, pagination and optional row selection, built on `Table`
- [Date picker](llms/date_picker.md): The DatePicker component is used to display a date input and a Calendar popover, allowing users to enter or select a date value
- [Dialog](llms/dialog.md): The dialog component can be used to display additional information or actions related to an item
- [Drag and drop list](llms/drag_and_drop_list.md): Allows users to create vertically sortable lists supporting drag and drop, touch or keyboard input
- [Drawer](llms/drawer.md): A panel that slides up from the bottom and can be dragged down to dismiss
- [Dropdown menu](llms/dropdown_menu.md): The DropdownMenu component is used to create a dropdown menu that can be triggered by a button click
- [Dropzone](llms/dropzone.md): A file picker you can also drop files onto
- [Empty](llms/empty.md): Placeholder for a list, table or page with nothing in it, with optional icon, text and actions
- [Field](llms/field.md): Wires a label, description and error to a control with matching ids
- [Form](llms/form.md): Validation state for a form, with the accessibility wiring done for you
- [Hooks](llms/hooks.md): Hooks shared by the components and by apps
- [Hover card](llms/hover_card.md): The HoverCard component can be used to display additional information when a user hovers over an element
- [Icons](llms/icons.md): The kit's one icon set: every Lucide icon, generated into Rust as shape data plus one component per icon, so apps and components import icons from one place
- [Input](llms/input.md): The input element is used to accept a text input from the user
- [InputGroup](llms/input_group.md): An input with text, icons or buttons attached inside one bordered box
- [InputOtp](llms/input_otp.md): A one-time-code input: one box per character
- [Item](llms/item.md): A versatile component for displaying content with media, title, description, and actions
- [Kbd](llms/kbd.md): A keyboard key cap, for showing shortcuts
- [Label](llms/label.md): The Label component is used to provide a label for form elements, enhancing accessibility and usability
- [Link](llms/link.md): `TextLink`: an inline text link, a plain `<a href>` with an underline, the kit's text colour and a visible focus ring
- [Marquee](llms/marquee.md): A looping auto-scrolling strip (logos, quotes)
- [Menubar](llms/menubar.md): The Menubar component can be used to display a menu bar with collapsible menus
- [MultiSelect](llms/multi_select.md): Pick several options from a list
- [Navbar](llms/navbar.md): The Navbar component can be used to display a navigation bar with collapsible sections
- [NumberField](llms/number_field.md): `NumberInput` is a number with - and + buttons, for counts and amounts (guests, quantity, nights)
- [Pagination](llms/pagination.md): The pagination component provides navigational controls for paged content
- [Popover](llms/popover.md): The Popover primitive provides an interactive modal that is positioned relative to the target element
- [Progress](llms/progress.md): The Progress component is used to display the progress of a task or operation
- [Radio group](llms/radio_group.md): The RadioGroup component is used to create a group of radio buttons that allows the user to select one option from a set
- [Scroll area](llms/scroll_area.md): The ScrollArea component is used to create a scrollable container for its children
- [Select](llms/select.md): The Select component is used to create a dropdown menu that allows users to select one or more options from the select groups
- [Separator](llms/separator.md): The Separator component is a simple horizontal or vertical line that can be used to visually separate content in your application
- [Sheet](llms/sheet.md): The sheet component is a panel that slides in from the edge of the screen
- [Shimmer](llms/shimmer.md): Wraps loading content and sweeps a highlight across it
- [Sidebar](llms/sidebar.md): The Sidebar component is a vertical interface panel fixed to the screen edge, displaying navigation menus or filters that enable quick access to different sections of an application
- [Skeleton](llms/skeleton.md): The Skeleton component is used to display a placeholder preview of content before the data gets loaded
- [SkipLink](llms/skip_link.md): `SkipLink` is a "Skip to content" link that stays hidden until it has keyboard focus, then appears in the corner, so keyboard users can jump past the header and navigation
- [Slider](llms/slider.md): The slider component allows users to select a value from a range by sliding a handle along a track
- [Spinner](llms/spinner.md): A loading indicator
- [Status](llms/status.md): A coloured dot plus required text label (idle, online, degraded, down)
- [Stepper](llms/stepper.md): A multi-step progress indicator with Back/Next control via `use_stepper()`
- [Switch](llms/switch.md): The Switch component allows users to toggle between two states, such as on and off
- [Table](llms/table.md): A styled table
- [Tabs](llms/tabs.md): The Tabs component is used to create a tabbed interface, allowing users to switch between different views or sections of content
- [Tag group](llms/tag_group.md): A Tag Group is a focusable group of tags (labels, categories, filters and similar items) with keyboard navigation, optional selection and removal
- [Textarea](llms/textarea.md): The textarea element is used to allow users to enter multi-line text input in a user interface
- [ThemeCustomizer](llms/theme_customizer.md): Pick an accent colour, corner radius and light/dark mode for the whole page
- [Toast](llms/toast.md): The Toast component is used to display brief messages to the user, typically for notifications or alerts
- [Toggle](llms/toggle.md): The Toggle component is used to create a toggle button that can be pressed or unpressed
- [Toggle group](llms/toggle_group.md): The Toggle Group component is used to create a group of toggle buttons that allows the user to select one or more options from a set
- [Toolbar](llms/toolbar.md): The toolbar component is a flexible and customizable component that can be used to create a variety of toolbars
- [Tooltip](llms/tooltip.md): The Tooltip component is used to display additional information when a user hovers over an element
- [UiStrings](llms/ui_strings.md): Every word the kit shows or announces on its own ("Next", "Clear", "No results found.", "Go to next page", screen-reader names) lives in one `UiStrings` struct with English defaults
- [Virtual list](llms/virtual_list.md): The VirtualList component virtualizes large lists by rendering only visible rows plus a buffer

# Accordion

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add accordion` or `dx components add accordion --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::accordion::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The accordion component is used to display collapsible content panels for presenting information in a limited amount of space. It allows users to expand and collapse sections to view more or less content.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The accordion component must wrap all accordion items.
Accordion {
    // Each accordion item contains both a trigger the expanded contents of the item.
    AccordionItem {
        // Each item must have an index starting from 0 to control where the item is placed.
        index: 0,
        // The trigger is used to expand or collapse the item.
        AccordionTrigger {}
        // The content that is shown when the item is expanded.
        AccordionContent {}
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Accordion(props: AccordionProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AccordionItem(props: AccordionItemProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AccordionTrigger(props: AccordionTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AccordionContent(props: AccordionContentProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::accordion::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let items = [
        (
            "Is it accessible?",
            "Yes. Behaviour comes from dioxus-primitives, which follows WAI-ARIA.",
        ),
        (
            "Is it styled?",
            "Yes. It ships with a neutral, shadcn-like theme you own.",
        ),
        (
            "Is it animated?",
            "Open and close are animated in CSS; springs arrive in week 2.",
        ),
    ];
    rsx! {
        div { style: "max-width: 32rem;",
            Accordion { allow_multiple_open: false, horizontal: false,
                for (i, (q, a)) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
                    AccordionItem { index: i,
                        AccordionTrigger { {q} }
                        AccordionContent {
                            p { style: "margin: 0; padding-bottom: 1rem;", {a} }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Alert

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add alert` or `dx components add alert --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::alert::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A message that interrupts: it is announced as soon as it appears. Use `Callout` for a quiet inline note.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="alert"`
- Keyboard: none (not interactive)
- Reduced motion: none

## API

```rust
pub enum AlertVariant {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Destructive,
}

/// A callout. Announced to screen readers (`role="alert"`) when it appears.
#[component]
pub fn Alert(
    #[props(default)] variant: AlertVariant,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertTitle(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertDescription(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::alert::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem; max-width: 28rem;",
            Alert {
                AlertTitle { "Heads up" }
                AlertDescription { "You can add components to your app with the registry." }
            }
            Alert { variant: AlertVariant::Destructive,
                AlertTitle { "Something went wrong" }
                AlertDescription { "Your session has expired. Sign in again to continue." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Alert dialog

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add alert_dialog` or `dx components add alert_dialog --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::alert_dialog::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The AlertDialog primitive provides an accessible, composable modal dialog for critical user confirmations (such as destructive actions).

## Component Structure

```rust
let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
rsx! {
    button { onclick: move |_| open.set(true), type: "button", "Show Alert Dialog" }
    AlertDialog { open: open(), on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
        AlertDialogTitle { "Title" }
        AlertDialogDescription { "Description" }
        AlertDialogActions {
            AlertDialogCancel { "Cancel" }
            AlertDialogAction { on_click: move |_| { /* destructive action */ }, "Confirm" }
        }
    }
}
```

### Components
- **AlertDialog**: Provides context, manages open state, renders the backdrop and the content panel.
- **AlertDialogTitle**: The dialog's heading.
- **AlertDialogDescription**: Additional description for the dialog.
- **AlertDialogActions**: Container for action buttons.
- **AlertDialogAction**: Main action button (e.g., confirm/delete). Closes the dialog, *then* calls the optional `on_click`. So if `on_open_change(false)` clears state (such as "which item to delete"), `on_click` sees it already cleared: keep that state separate from the open flag.
- **AlertDialogCancel**: Cancel/close button. Closes dialog and calls optional `on_click`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn AlertDialog(props: AlertDialogRootProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertDialogTitle(props: AlertDialogTitleProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertDialogDescription(props: AlertDialogDescriptionProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertDialogActions(props: AlertDialogActionsProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertDialogCancel(props: AlertDialogCancelProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn AlertDialogAction(props: AlertDialogActionProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;

use crate::components::alert_dialog::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut confirmed = use_signal(|| false);

    rsx! {
        Button {
            r#type: "button",
            "data-style": "outline",
            style: "margin-bottom: 1.5rem;",
            onclick: move |_| open.set(true),
            "Show Alert Dialog"
        }
        AlertDialog { open: open(), on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            AlertDialogTitle { "Delete item" }
            AlertDialogDescription { "Are you sure you want to delete this item? This action cannot be undone." }
            AlertDialogActions {
                AlertDialogCancel { "Cancel" }
                AlertDialogAction { on_click: move |_| confirmed.set(true), "Delete" }
            }
        }
        if confirmed() {
            p { style: "color: var(--contrast-error-color); margin-top: 16px; font-weight: 600;",
                "Item deleted!"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Aspect ratio

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add aspect_ratio` or `dx components add aspect_ratio --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::aspect_ratio::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The AspectRatio component is used to maintain a specific aspect ratio for its children. This is particularly useful for responsive designs where you want to ensure that an element retains its proportions regardless of the screen size.

## Component Structure

```rust
AspectRatio {
    // The aspect ratio to maintain (width / height)
    ratio: 4. / 3.,
    // The children of the AspectRatio component will be rendered within it.
    {children}
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn AspectRatio(props: AspectRatioProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::aspect_ratio::AspectRatio;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[css_module("/src/components/aspect_ratio/style.css")]
struct Styles;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div {
            class: Styles::dx_aspect_ratio_container,
            width: "20rem",
            max_width: "30vw",
            AspectRatio { ratio: 4.0 / 3.0,
                div {
                    background: "linear-gradient(to bottom right, var(--primary-color-5), var(--primary-color-3))",
                    width: "100%",
                    height: "100%",
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Avatar

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add avatar` or `dx components add avatar --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::avatar::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Avatar components display a user's profile picture or fallback initials. Use the composable `Avatar`, `AvatarImage`, and `AvatarFallback` primitives when you need full control, or `ImageAvatar` for the common image-with-fallback case.

## Component Structure

```rust
Avatar {
    label: "Jane Doe",
    AvatarImage {
        src: "https://example.com/avatar.png",
        alt: "Jane Doe",
    }
    AvatarFallback { "JD" }
}
```

```rust
ImageAvatar {
    src: "https://example.com/avatar.png",
    alt: "Jane Doe",
    on_state_change: |state: AvatarState| { /* image is loading/loaded/failed */ },
    "JD"
}
```

## Naming

The avatar is `role="img"`, so a screen reader reads its name, never the initials inside. `label` names it (`ImageAvatar` uses `alt` when there is no `label`). An avatar with no `label`, `alt`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is decorative: it renders `aria-hidden="true"`, which is right when the person's name is shown next to it.

## API

```rust
pub enum AvatarImageSize {
    #[default]
    Small,
    Medium,
    Large,
}

pub enum AvatarShape {
    #[default]
    Circle,
    Rounded,
}

/// The props for the [`Avatar`] root component.
pub struct AvatarProps {
    /// Callback when image loads successfully.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_load: Option<EventHandler<()>>,

    /// Callback when image fails to load.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_error: Option<EventHandler<()>>,

    /// Callback when the avatar state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_state_change: Option<EventHandler<AvatarState>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub size: AvatarImageSize,

    #[props(default)]
    pub shape: AvatarShape,

    /// The person or thing shown, read by screen readers ("Ada Lovelace"). The avatar is
    /// `role="img"`, so neither the image's `alt` nor the fallback initials name it. Without
    /// a `label` (or an `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`), the avatar is decorative and
    /// hidden from assistive technology: use that when the name is shown beside it.
    #[props(default, into)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes for the avatar element.
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The fallback content shown while the image is loading or if it fails to load.
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Avatar(props: AvatarProps) -> Element

pub struct AvatarImageProps {
    #[props(default)]
    pub id: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    pub src: String,

    #[props(default)]
    pub alt: String,

    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

#[component]
pub fn AvatarImage(props: AvatarImageProps) -> Element

pub struct AvatarFallbackProps {
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn AvatarFallback(props: AvatarFallbackProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ImageAvatar`] convenience component.
pub struct ImageAvatarProps {
    /// The image source URL.
    pub src: String,

    /// The image alt text.
    #[props(default)]
    pub alt: String,

    /// Callback when image loads successfully.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_load: Option<EventHandler<()>>,

    /// Callback when image fails to load.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_error: Option<EventHandler<()>>,

    /// Callback when the avatar state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_state_change: Option<EventHandler<AvatarState>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub size: AvatarImageSize,

    #[props(default)]
    pub shape: AvatarShape,

    /// The person or thing shown, read by screen readers ("Ada Lovelace"). The avatar is
    /// `role="img"`, so neither the image's `alt` nor the fallback initials name it. Without
    /// a `label` (or an `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`), the avatar is decorative and
    /// hidden from assistive technology: use that when the name is shown beside it.
    #[props(default, into)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes for the avatar element.
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The fallback content shown while the image is loading or if it fails to load.
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ImageAvatar(props: ImageAvatarProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::avatar::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

/// A neutral placeholder image (an inline SVG) for avatar demos, so demos never hit the network.
pub const DEMO_AVATAR_SRC: &str = concat!(
    "data:image/svg+xml;utf8,",
    "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'>",
    "<rect width='64' height='64' fill='%23888'/>",
    "<circle cx='32' cy='25' r='11' fill='%23fff'/>",
    "<path d='M10 58c3-15 13-21 22-21s19 6 22 21z' fill='%23fff'/></svg>"
);

#[css_module("/src/components/avatar/style.css")]
struct Styles;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut avatar_state = use_signal(|| "No state yet".to_string());
    rsx! {
        div {
            display: "flex",
            flex_direction: "row",
            align_items: "center",
            justify_content: "center",
            flex_wrap: "wrap",
            gap: "1rem",
            div { class: Styles::dx_avatar_item,
                p { class: Styles::dx_avatar_label, "Basic Usage" }
                ImageAvatar {
                    size: AvatarImageSize::Small,
                    src: DEMO_AVATAR_SRC,
                    alt: "User avatar",
                    on_state_change: move |state| {
                        avatar_state.set(format!("Avatar 1: {state:?}"));
                    },
                    aria_label: "Basic avatar",
                    "EA"
                }
            }
            div { class: Styles::dx_avatar_item,
                p { class: Styles::dx_avatar_label, "Rounded" }
                ImageAvatar {
                    size: AvatarImageSize::Small,
                    shape: AvatarShape::Rounded,
                    src: DEMO_AVATAR_SRC,
                    alt: "User avatar",
                    on_state_change: move |state| {
                        avatar_state.set(format!("Avatar 2: {state:?}"));
                    },
                    aria_label: "Basic avatar",
                    "EA"
                }
            }
            div { class: Styles::dx_avatar_item,
                p { class: Styles::dx_avatar_label, "Error State" }
                ImageAvatar {
                    size: AvatarImageSize::Medium,
                    src: "/does-not-exist.png",
                    alt: "Invalid image",
                    on_state_change: move |state| {
                        avatar_state.set(format!("Avatar 3: {state:?}"));
                    },
                    aria_label: "Error avatar",
                    "JK"
                }
            }
            div { class: Styles::dx_avatar_item,
                p { class: Styles::dx_avatar_label, "Large Size" }
                ImageAvatar {
                    size: AvatarImageSize::Large,
                    src: DEMO_AVATAR_SRC.to_string(),
                    alt: "Large avatar",
                    on_state_change: move |state| {
                        avatar_state.set(format!("Avatar 4: {state:?}"));
                    },
                    aria_label: "Large avatar",
                    "DX"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Badge

The Badge is a component designed to display small, distinct labels that help highlight important content or status indicators. Perfect for use cases like notifications, status labels, or categorization.

## Component Structure

Badge {
    {children}
}

    Outline,

}

#[component]
pub fn Badge(props: BadgeProps) -> Element

# BottomNav

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add bottom_nav` or `dx components add bottom_nav --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::bottom_nav::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A mobile-style tab bar of links or buttons.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `nav` landmark named by `label`; the active item has `aria-current="page"`; icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Keyboard: Tab through items; links or buttons
- Reduced motion: none

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`bottom_nav.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
/// A mobile-style tab bar fixed to the bottom of its container. Wrap [`BottomNavItem`]s;
/// `label` names the landmark (for example "Main").
#[component]
pub fn BottomNav(
    #[props(into)] label: Option<String>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// One destination. With `href` it renders a link, otherwise a button. `current` marks the
/// active page (`aria-current="page"`).
#[component]
pub fn BottomNavItem(
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] href: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] current: bool,
    #[props(default)] onclick: Callback<MouseEvent>,
    /// Decorative icon; hidden from assistive tech.
    #[props(default)]
    icon: Option<Element>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::bottom_nav::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut current = use_signal(|| 0_usize);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "max-width: 24rem; border: 1px solid var(--primary-color-6); border-radius: var(--radius); overflow: hidden;",
            BottomNav { label: "Demo tabs",
                for (index , name) in ["Home", "Search", "Inbox"].into_iter().enumerate() {
                    BottomNavItem {
                        label: name,
                        current: current() == index,
                        onclick: move |_| current.set(index),
                        icon: rsx! {
                            svg {
                                view_box: "0 0 24 24",
                                fill: "none",
                                stroke: "currentColor",
                                stroke_width: "2",
                                circle { cx: "12", cy: "12", r: "8" }
                            }
                        },
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Breadcrumb

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add breadcrumb` or `dx components add breadcrumb --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `hooks`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::breadcrumb::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A trail of links to the current page.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the current page is not a link and has `aria-current="page"`; separators are `aria-hidden`
- Keyboard: links are tabbable in order
- Reduced motion: none

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Breadcrumb(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn BreadcrumbItem(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn BreadcrumbLink(
    #[props(into, default = "#".to_string())] href: String,
    /// For in-app navigation without a router: call `prevent_default()` and switch the view.
    /// With the kit's `router` feature, a path `href` goes through the router by itself.
    #[props(default)]
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// The current page: not a link, and marked with `aria-current="page"`.
#[component]
pub fn BreadcrumbPage(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// The divider between items. Hidden from assistive technology.
#[component]
pub fn BreadcrumbSeparator() -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::breadcrumb::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Breadcrumb {
            BreadcrumbItem { BreadcrumbLink { href: "#", "Home" } }
            BreadcrumbSeparator {}
            BreadcrumbItem { BreadcrumbLink { href: "#", "Components" } }
            BreadcrumbSeparator {}
            BreadcrumbItem { BreadcrumbPage { "Breadcrumb" } }
        }
    }
}
```

# Button

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add button` or `dx components add button --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::button::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The button element is used to trigger actions or events in a user interface.

For a link that should look like a button (the router's `Link`, which renders its own `<a>`), spread `button_look(variant, size)` onto it: `Link { to: Route::Trips {}, attributes: button_look(ButtonVariant::Outline, ButtonSize::Default), "My trips" }`. Don't also pass `class`. A link keeps link semantics: it navigates on Enter, not Space.

## Component Structure

```rust
button {
    // Global html attributes
    class: "dx-button",
    "data-style": "outline",
    "data-size": "default",
    // Children
    {children}
}
```

## API

```rust
pub enum ButtonVariant {
    #[default]
    Primary,
    Secondary,
    Destructive,
    Outline,
    Ghost,
    Link,
}

pub enum ButtonSize {
    Xs,
    Sm,
    #[default]
    Default,
    Lg,
    Icon,
    IconXs,
    IconSm,
    IconLg,
}

/// A [`Button`]'s look for an element that is not a `<button>`, such as the router's `Link`
/// (which renders its own `<a>`):
/// `Link { to: Route::Trips {}, attributes: button_look(ButtonVariant::Outline, ButtonSize::Default), "My trips" }`.
/// Don't also pass `class` to that element: it would replace the button class.
pub fn button_look(variant: ButtonVariant, size: ButtonSize) -> Vec<Attribute>

#[component]
pub fn Button(
    #[props(default)] variant: ButtonVariant,
    #[props(default)] size: ButtonSize,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=button)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmousedown: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmouseup: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onkeydown: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Button { "Primary" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Secondary, "Secondary" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Outline" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Ghost, "Ghost" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Destructive, "Delete" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Link, "Link" }
        }
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; margin-top: 0.75rem;",
            Button { size: ButtonSize::Xs, "Extra small" }
            Button { size: ButtonSize::Sm, "Small" }
            Button { "Default" }
            Button { size: ButtonSize::Lg, "Large" }
            Button { disabled: true, "Disabled" }
        }
    }
}
```

# ButtonGroup

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add button_group` or `dx components add button_group --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::button_group::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Joins buttons or inputs into a segmented control, horizontal or vertical.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="group"`; pass an `aria-label`.
- Keyboard: normal Tab order; focused item is raised above its neighbours
- Reduced motion: none

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`button_group.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
/// Joins `Button`s (and inputs) into one segmented control. Give it an `aria-label` so the
/// group is announced; it carries `role="group"`.
#[component]
pub fn ButtonGroup(
    #[props(default)] vertical: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// A non-interactive label segment inside a `ButtonGroup`.
#[component]
pub fn ButtonGroupText(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::button_group::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1.5rem; align-items: flex-start;",
            ButtonGroup { "aria-label": "Text alignment",
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Left" }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Center" }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Right" }
            }
            ButtonGroup { vertical: true, "aria-label": "Zoom",
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Zoom in" }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Zoom out" }
            }
            ButtonGroup { "aria-label": "Page size",
                ButtonGroupText { "Rows" }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "10" }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "25" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Calendar

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add calendar` or `dx components add calendar --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::calendar::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Calendar component is used to display a calendar interface, allowing users to select dates. It provides a grid layout of days for a specific month and year.

## Component Structure

```rust
Calendar {
    // The currently selected date in the calendar (if any).
    selected_date,
    on_date_change: |date: Option<CalendarDate>| {
        // This callback is triggered when a date is selected in the calendar.
        // The date parameter contains the selected date.
    },
    // The current view date of the calendar, which determines the month and year displayed.
    view_date,
    on_view_change: |date: CalendarDate| {
        // This callback is triggered when the view date changes.
        // The date parameter contains the new view date.
    },
    // Optional number of pre-composed month views to render.
    month_count: 1,
}
```

The styled `Calendar` and `RangeCalendar` render a complete month view by default, including the header, navigation, month/year selectors, and date grid.

## API

```rust
pub struct CalendarProps {
    /// The selected date
    #[props(default)]
    pub selected_date: ReadSignal<Option<Date>>,

    /// Callback when selected date changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_date_change: Callback<Option<Date>>,

    /// Callback when display weekday
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|weekday: Weekday| weekday_abbreviation(weekday).to_string()))]
    pub on_format_weekday: Callback<Weekday, String>,

    /// Callback when display month
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|month: Month| month.to_string()))]
    pub on_format_month: Callback<Month, String>,

    /// The month being viewed
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(UtcDateTime::now().date())))]
    pub view_date: ReadSignal<Date>,

    /// The current date (used for highlighting today)
    #[props(default = UtcDateTime::now().date())]
    pub today: Date,

    /// Callback when view date changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_view_change: Callback<Date>,

    /// Whether the calendar is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// First day of the week
    #[props(default = Weekday::Sunday)]
    pub first_day_of_week: Weekday,

    /// Lower limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(1925, Month::January, 1))]
    pub min_date: Date,

    /// Upper limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(2050, Month::December, 31))]
    pub max_date: Date,

    /// Specify how many months are visible at once
    #[props(default = 1)]
    pub month_count: u8,

    /// Unavailable dates
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled_ranges: ReadSignal<Vec<calendar::DateRange>>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the calendar element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

pub struct RangeCalendarProps {
    /// The selected range
    #[props(default)]
    pub selected_range: ReadSignal<Option<calendar::DateRange>>,

    /// Callback when selected date range changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_range_change: Callback<Option<calendar::DateRange>>,

    /// Callback when display weekday
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|weekday: Weekday| weekday_abbreviation(weekday).to_string()))]
    pub on_format_weekday: Callback<Weekday, String>,

    /// Callback when display month
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|month: Month| month.to_string()))]
    pub on_format_month: Callback<Month, String>,

    /// The month being viewed
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(UtcDateTime::now().date())))]
    pub view_date: ReadSignal<Date>,

    /// The current date (used for highlighting today)
    #[props(default = UtcDateTime::now().date())]
    pub today: Date,

    /// Callback when view date changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_view_change: Callback<Date>,

    /// Whether the calendar is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// First day of the week
    #[props(default = Weekday::Sunday)]
    pub first_day_of_week: Weekday,

    /// Lower limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(1925, Month::January, 1))]
    pub min_date: Date,

    /// Upper limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(2050, Month::December, 31))]
    pub max_date: Date,

    /// Specify how many months are visible at once
    #[props(default = 1)]
    pub month_count: u8,

    /// Unavailable dates
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled_ranges: ReadSignal<Vec<calendar::DateRange>>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the calendar element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

#[component]
pub fn Calendar(props: CalendarProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn RangeCalendar(props: RangeCalendarProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::calendar::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use time::{macros::date, Date};

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut selected_date = use_signal(|| None::<Date>);
    let mut view_date = use_signal(|| date!(2026 - 05 - 15));
    rsx! {
        div { style: "padding: 20px;",
            Calendar {
                selected_date: selected_date(),
                on_date_change: move |date| {
                    tracing::info!("Selected date: {:?}", date);
                    selected_date.set(date);
                },
                view_date: view_date(),
                on_view_change: move |new_view: Date| {
                    tracing::info!("View changed to: {}-{}", new_view.year(), new_view.month());
                    view_date.set(new_view);
                },
                min_date: date!(1995 - 07 - 21),
                max_date: date!(2035 - 09 - 11),
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Callout

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add callout` or `dx components add callout --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::callout::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

An inline note (info, success, warning) for docs and forms. Static: use `Alert` for messages that must interrupt.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="note"`; the optional title is a paragraph.
- Keyboard: none (not interactive)
- Reduced motion: none

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`callout.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
pub enum CalloutVariant {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Info,
    Success,
    Warning,
}

/// An inline note for docs and forms. Unlike `Alert` it is not announced when it appears, so use
/// it for static content; use `Alert` for messages that must interrupt.
#[component]
pub fn Callout(
    #[props(default)] variant: CalloutVariant,
    /// Optional bold heading.
    #[props(into, default)]
    title: Option<String>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::callout::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem; max-width: 32rem;",
            Callout { title: "Heads up", "Callouts are static notes. Use " code { "Alert" } " to interrupt." }
            Callout { variant: CalloutVariant::Info, title: "Tip", "Press / to open the command palette." }
            Callout { variant: CalloutVariant::Success, "Saved. Your changes are live." }
            Callout { variant: CalloutVariant::Warning, title: "Careful", "This replaces the existing file." }
        }
    }
}
```

# Card

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add card` or `dx components add card --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::card::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The card component is a flexible container for grouping related content and actions. It provides a structured layout with optional header, content, and footer sections.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Card component must wrap all card elements.
Card {
    // CardHeader contains the title, description, and optional action.
    CardHeader {
        // CardTitle displays the main heading.
        CardTitle { "Card Title" }
        // CardDescription provides supporting text.
        CardDescription { "Card description goes here." }
        // CardAction positions action elements (e.g., buttons) in the header.
        CardAction {
            Button { "Action" }
        }
    }
    // CardContent holds the main body content.
    CardContent {
        p { "Main content of the card." }
    }
    // CardFooter contains footer actions or information.
    CardFooter {
        Button { "Submit" }
    }
}
```

## Layout Notes

- When `CardAction` is present inside `CardHeader`, the header automatically switches to a two-column grid layout.
- `CardMedia` holds an edge-to-edge image: put it first (or last) and it meets the card's edge with the card's rounded corners, no negative margins needed. An `img` inside is cropped to fill it.
- The card's corner radius is twice the theme `--radius` (1rem by default), so the theme's radius setting reaches cards.

```rust
Card {
    CardMedia { img { src: "/cabin.jpg", alt: "The cabin from the lake", style: "aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;" } }
    CardHeader { CardTitle { "Lakeside cabin" } }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Card(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CardHeader(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CardTitle(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CardDescription(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CardAction(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// An edge-to-edge image, video or map in a card: no side padding, and as the first (or
/// last) child it meets the card's top (or bottom) edge with the card's rounded corners.
/// An `img` inside is cropped to fill it; give it an `alt`.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn CardMedia(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CardContent(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CardFooter(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::card::*;
use crate::components::input::Input;
use crate::components::label::Label;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Card { style: "width: 100%; max-width: 24rem;",
            CardHeader {
                CardTitle { "Create project" }
                CardDescription { "Deploy your new project in one click." }
            }
            CardContent {
                div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 20rem;",
                    Label { html_for: "gallery-project", "Project name" }
                    Input { id: "gallery-project", placeholder: "my-app" }
                }
            }
            CardFooter { style: "justify-content: space-between;",
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Cancel" }
                Button { "Create" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Carousel

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add carousel` or `dx components add carousel --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::carousel::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A horizontally scrolling row of slides with scroll snapping and Previous/Next buttons. Nothing auto-plays, so there is no motion to pause.

```rust
Carousel { label: "Featured plans",
    CarouselItem { label: "1 of 3", "..." }
    CarouselItem { label: "2 of 3", "..." }
}
```

Slide width and spacing are CSS (`.dx-carousel-item` flex-basis); the buttons scroll by about one viewport. Slides centre their content; `CarouselItem { media: true, img { .. } }` makes a full-bleed photo slide instead (the content fills the slide and an `img` is cropped to cover it).

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `section` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` named by `label`; the scrolling track is a focusable group; each slide is `aria-roledescription="slide"` with your `label`.
- Keyboard: focus the track and use the arrow keys (native scrolling), or Tab to the Previous/Next buttons.
- Reduced motion: scrolling is instant instead of smooth.

## Source

Original to this repo. The pattern follows the WAI-ARIA carousel practices; Rust/UI's `carousel.rs` was used only to see the feature set.

## API

```rust
/// A row of slides that scrolls horizontally and snaps, with Previous/Next buttons. The track
/// itself is focusable, so arrow keys scroll it. Nothing moves on its own.
#[component]
pub fn Carousel(
    /// Accessible name, for example "Featured products".
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// One slide. Give it a `label` such as "1 of 4" so screen readers can place it.
#[component]
pub fn CarouselItem(
    #[props(into, default)] label: Option<String>,
    /// A full-bleed slide for a photo or video: the content fills the slide edge to edge
    /// (an `img` is cropped to cover it) instead of being centred.
    #[props(default)]
    media: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::carousel::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "max-width: 32rem;",
            Carousel { label: "Featured plans",
                for (i , name) in ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise"].into_iter().enumerate() {
                    CarouselItem { label: "{i + 1} of 4", strong { "{name}" } }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Chart

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add chart` or `dx components add chart --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::chart::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

`BarChart` and `LineChart` drawn as SVG from a list of `ChartDatum`. `describe()` builds the text alternative.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="img"` with an `aria-label` summarising the data
- Keyboard: none (not interactive)
- Reduced motion: none

## Stability

Experimental. Multi-series charts and a legend are planned and will change the props; see `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## API

```rust
/// One point or bar.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct ChartDatum {
    pub label: String,
    pub value: f32,
}

/// Round `max` up to a "nice" axis limit (1, 2, 5 or 10 times a power of ten).
/// Non-positive and non-finite input gives 1, so an empty chart still has an axis.
pub fn nice_max(max: f32) -> f32

/// A plain-language summary for screen readers, since an SVG chart has no text structure.
pub fn describe(data: &[ChartDatum]) -> String

/// A bar chart drawn as SVG in the accent colour. `label` is read by screen readers along
/// with a summary of every value; hovering a bar shows its value.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn BarChart(
    data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default = 200.0)] height: f32,
) -> Element

/// A line chart drawn as SVG with theme colors. Same accessibility contract as [`BarChart`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn LineChart(
    data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default = 200.0)] height: f32,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::chart::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

fn monthly() -> Vec<ChartDatum> {
    [
        ("Jan", 186.0),
        ("Feb", 305.0),
        ("Mar", 237.0),
        ("Apr", 73.0),
        ("May", 209.0),
        ("Jun", 214.0),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .map(|(label, value)| ChartDatum::new(label, value))
    .collect()
}

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 2rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr));",
            BarChart { data: monthly(), label: "Visitors per month, January to June" }
            LineChart { data: monthly(), label: "Visitors per month, January to June (line)" }
        }
    }
}
```

// The checkbox component creates a checkbox button

# Chips

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add chips` or `dx components add chips --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::chips::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A row of on/off chips for filters and multi-choice tags. Each chip is a native checkbox inside its label; a check mark appears when it is on.

```rust
Chips { label: "Filter by status",
    Chip { default_checked: true, "Open" }
    Chip { "In review" }
    Chip { checked: done(), on_change: move |v| done.set(v), "Done" }
}
```

For one choice out of several, use `ToggleGroup` or `RadioGroup` instead.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="group"` named by `label`; each chip is a native checkbox named by its text
- Keyboard: Tab moves between chips, Space toggles
- State: announced as checked or not checked, and shown with a check mark as well as colour; forced-colors mode outlines the selected chip
- Reduced motion: the check mark and colour change without transition

## Source

Idea from Rust/UI `chips.rs` (rust-ui/ui@43ddc65, MIT). Rewritten: upstream hides the checkbox with `display: none` (unreachable by keyboard and screen readers) and styles with Tailwind; here the checkbox stays focusable and the styles use theme tokens.

## API

```rust
/// A labelled group of [`Chip`]s, for filters and multi-choice tags.
#[component]
pub fn Chips(
    /// Names the group for screen readers, e.g. "Filter by status".
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// One on/off chip: a native checkbox inside its label, so Tab reaches it, Space toggles it
/// and screen readers announce "checked". A check mark shows the state as well as the colour.
///
/// Uncontrolled with `default_checked`, or controlled with `checked` plus `on_change`.
#[component]
pub fn Chip(
    /// Controlled state. Leave unset to let the chip keep its own.
    checked: Option<bool>,
    /// Starting state when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    default_checked: bool,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Form field name and value, when the chips sit in a `<form>`.
    #[props(into)]
    name: Option<String>,
    #[props(into)] value: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] on_change: EventHandler<bool>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::chips::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut done = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Chips { label: "Filter by status",
                Chip { default_checked: true, "Open" }
                Chip { "In review" }
                Chip { checked: done(), on_change: move |v| done.set(v), "Done" }
                Chip { disabled: true, "Archived" }
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--secondary-color-5);",
                if done() { "Showing done tasks." } else { "Hiding done tasks." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Collapsible

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add collapsible` or `dx components add collapsible --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::collapsible::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The `Collapsible` component allows users to create expandable sections that can be toggled open or closed. This is useful for displaying content in a compact manner, such as FAQs, menus, or any content that benefits from being hidden until needed.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The collapsible component must wrap all collapsible items.
Collapsible {
    // The trigger is used to expand or collapse the item.
    CollapsibleTrigger {}
    // The content that is shown when the item is expanded.
    CollapsibleContent {}
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Collapsible(props: CollapsibleProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleTrigger(props: CollapsibleTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleContent(props: CollapsibleContentProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleItem(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleList(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::collapsible::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Collapsible {
            CollapsibleTrigger {
                b { "Recent Activity" }
            }
            CollapsibleList {
                CollapsibleItem { "Added a new feature to the collapsible component" }
                CollapsibleContent {
                    CollapsibleItem { "Fixed a bug in the collapsible component" }
                    CollapsibleItem { "Updated the documentation for the collapsible component" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Color picker

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add color_picker` or `dx components add color_picker --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `input`).
- Import: `use crate::components::color_picker::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Color picker used when the user needs to make a customized color selection.

## Component Structure

```rust
ColorPicker {
    // The currently selected color in the color picker.
    color,
    on_color_change: move |c: Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>| {
        // This callback is triggered when a color is selected in the popover.
        // The HSV parameter contains the selected color.
    },

    // Optional label on the trigger button.
    label: "Pick",
}
```

### Custom Popover

`ColorPicker` renders the default trigger and `ColorPickerSelect` content. If you
want to fully replace the default popover UI, compose the picker from
`ColorPickerRoot`, `ColorPickerTrigger`, and `ColorPickerPopover`:

```rust
ColorPickerRoot {
    color,
    on_color_change: move |c: Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>| { /* ... */ },

    ColorPickerTrigger {
        label: "Pick",
    }

    ColorPickerPopover {
        div {
            "Custom color picker content"
        }
    }
}
```

If you only need to add content after the default controls, pass children to
`ColorPicker`; they will be appended inside the default popover.

## API

```rust
/// The props for the [`ColorPickerRoot`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerRootProps {
    /// The selected color
    #[props(default)]
    pub color: ReadSignal<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Callback when color changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_color_change: Callback<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Whether the color picker is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The controlled open state of the popover.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default open state when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Callback fired when the open state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color picker element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color picker element
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerRoot(props: ColorPickerRootProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorPicker`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerProps {
    /// The selected color
    #[props(default)]
    pub color: ReadSignal<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Callback when color changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_color_change: Callback<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Whether the color picker is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Optional label on the trigger button
    #[props(default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// The controlled open state of the popover.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default open state when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Callback fired when the open state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color picker element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// Additional content to append to the default color picker popover
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPicker(props: ColorPickerProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorPickerTrigger`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerTriggerProps {
    /// Optional label on the trigger button
    #[props(default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the trigger button
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// Additional content to render inside the trigger button
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerTrigger(props: ColorPickerTriggerProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorPickerPopover`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerPopoverProps {
    /// Additional attributes to extend the popover content
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color picker popover
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerPopover(props: ColorPickerPopoverProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorField`] component.
pub struct ColorFieldProps {
    /// Optional label above the input field
    #[props(default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// Optional props for the text description element
    #[props(default)]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color field element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color field element
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The props for the [`ColorSwatch`] component.
pub struct ColorSwatchProps {
    /// The selected color
    #[props(default)]
    pub color: ReadSignal<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color swatch element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color swatch element
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The props for the [`ColorSlider`] component.
pub struct ColorSliderProps {
    pub title: ReadSignal<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color slider element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color slider element
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The props for the [`ColorPickerSelect`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerSelectProps {
    /// Additional attributes to extend the color picker select element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color picker select element
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerSelect(props: ColorPickerSelectProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;

use crate::components::color_picker::*;
use dioxus_primitives::color_picker::Color;
use palette::{encoding, Hsv, IntoColor};

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut color = use_signal(|| -> Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64> {
        Color::new(155, 128, 255).into_format::<f64>().into_color()
    });

    rsx! {
        ColorPicker {
            label: "Pick a color",
            color: color(),
            on_color_change: move |c| {
                tracing::info!("Color changed: {:?}", c);
                color.set(c);
            },
        }
    }
}
```

# Combobox

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add combobox` or `dx components add combobox --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::combobox::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Combobox component is an autocomplete input with a filterable popup list.

Filtering preserves the order defined by the rendered `ComboboxOption` elements and their `index`
props. If you want query-dependent ranking, control `query`, sort your item data in user code,
render the options in that sorted order, and assign indexes from the sorted list.

## Component Structure

```rust
let mut value = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
let mut query = use_signal(String::new);

Combobox::<String> {
    value: Some(value.into()),
    on_value_change: move |next: Option<String>| {
        value.set(next);
    },
    query: Some(query()),
    on_query_change: move |next| query.set(next),
    placeholder: "Select framework...",
    aria_label: "Select framework",
    list_aria_label: "Frameworks",
    ComboboxEmpty { "No framework found." }
    ComboboxOption::<String> {
        index: 0usize,
        value: "next".to_string(),
        text_value: "Next.js",
        "Next.js"
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
pub struct ComboboxProps<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static = String> {
    #[props(default)]
    pub value: Option<ReadSignal<Option<T>>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_value: Option<T>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_value_change: Callback<Option<T>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub query: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_query: ReadSignal<String>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_query_change: Callback<String>,

    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub roving_loop: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default = Callback::new(|(q, t): (String, String)| default_combobox_filter(&q, &t)))]
    pub filter: Callback<(String, String), bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub placeholder: ReadSignal<String>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub aria_label: Option<String>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub list_aria_label: Option<String>,

    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Combobox<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: ComboboxProps<T>) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ComboboxEmpty(props: ComboboxEmptyProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ComboboxOption<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: ComboboxOptionProps<T>) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::combobox::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut query = use_signal(String::new);
    let frameworks: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        ("next", "Next.js"),
        ("svelte", "SvelteKit"),
        ("nuxt", "Nuxt.js"),
        ("remix", "Remix"),
        ("astro", "Astro"),
        ("solid", "SolidStart"),
        ("dioxus", "Dioxus"),
    ];

    rsx! {
        Combobox::<String> {
            query: Some(query()),
            on_query_change: move |next| query.set(next),
            placeholder: "Select framework...",
            aria_label: "Select framework",
            list_aria_label: "Frameworks",
            ComboboxEmpty { "No framework found." }
            for (i , (value , label)) in frameworks.iter().enumerate() {
                ComboboxOption::<String> {
                    index: i,
                    value: value.to_string(),
                    text_value: label.to_string(),
                    {*label}
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Command

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add command` or `dx components add command --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `dialog`, `hooks`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::command::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A command palette: a search box over a filtered list, inside a dialog. `filter_items` and `step_active` are pure helpers.

Pass `hotkey: "k"` to open it with Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS); it uses `use_hotkey` from the `hooks` item, which `rust-ui add command` installs with it. That works on the web only, so keep a visible button too.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `combobox` input controlling a labelled `listbox`, with `aria-activedescendant` on the highlighted option
- Keyboard: Ctrl+K opens it (web, with `hotkey: "k"`); type to filter, Arrow keys move the highlight, Enter runs it, Escape closes
- Reduced motion: none

## API

```rust
/// One entry in a command palette.
pub struct CommandItem {
    pub id: String,
    pub label: String,
    /// Shown as a heading above consecutive items that share it.
    pub group: Option<String>,
    /// Display-only hint such as `Ctrl K`.
    pub shortcut: Option<String>,
}

/// Indices of the items that match `query`: every whitespace-separated word must appear in
/// the label, ignoring case. An empty query matches everything. Order is preserved.
pub fn filter_items(items: &[CommandItem], query: &str) -> Vec<usize>

/// Move the highlighted row by `delta`, wrapping at both ends. `len == 0` yields 0.
pub fn step_active(current: usize, delta: isize, len: usize) -> usize

/// Where the highlight goes after `key` in a list of `len` rows, or `None` if the key
/// doesn't move it. Arrows wrap; Home and End jump to the ends.
pub fn command_nav(key: &Key, active: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize>

/// A searchable list of actions in a modal dialog. Type to filter, arrow keys to move,
/// Enter to choose, Escape to close. Focus stays in the input; the highlighted row is
/// exposed through `aria-activedescendant`.
#[component]
pub fn CommandDialog(
    open: bool,
    on_open_change: EventHandler<bool>,
    items: Vec<CommandItem>,
    on_select: EventHandler<String>,
    /// Defaults to "Search commands..." ([`UiStrings`](crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings)).
    #[props(into)]
    placeholder: Option<String>,
    /// Open with Ctrl+`hotkey` (Cmd on macOS) anywhere on the page, e.g. `hotkey: "k"`.
    /// Web only ([`use_hotkey`]); keep a visible button that opens it too. Read once, on mount.
    hotkey: Option<&'static str>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::command::*;
use crate::components::kbd::{Kbd, KbdGroup};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut last = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
    let items = vec![
        CommandItem::new("new-file", "New file")
            .group("File")
            .shortcut("Ctrl N"),
        CommandItem::new("open-file", "Open file")
            .group("File")
            .shortcut("Ctrl O"),
        CommandItem::new("save-file", "Save file")
            .group("File")
            .shortcut("Ctrl S"),
        CommandItem::new("toggle-theme", "Toggle theme").group("View"),
        CommandItem::new("zoom-in", "Zoom in")
            .group("View")
            .shortcut("Ctrl +"),
        CommandItem::new("zoom-out", "Zoom out")
            .group("View")
            .shortcut("Ctrl -"),
    ];
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap;",
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| open.set(true),
                "Open command palette"
                KbdGroup {
                    Kbd { "Ctrl" }
                    Kbd { "K" }
                }
            }
            if let Some(id) = last() {
                span { style: "font-size: 0.875rem;", "Ran: {id}" }
            }
        }
        CommandDialog {
            open: open(),
            on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            items,
            on_select: move |id| last.set(Some(id)),
            // Ctrl+K (Cmd+K) anywhere on the page; the button does the same off the web.
            hotkey: "k",
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Context menu

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add context_menu` or `dx components add context_menu --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::context_menu::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The context menu component can be used to define a context menu that is displayed when the user right-clicks on an element. It can contain various menu items that the user can interact with.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The context menu component must wrap all context menu items.
ContextMenu {
    // The context menu trigger is the element that will display the context menu when right-clicked.
    ContextMenuTrigger {
        // The content of the trigger
        {children}
    }
    // The context menu content contains all the items that will be displayed in the context menu.
    ContextMenuContent {
        // Each context menu item represents an individual action in the context menu. Items are displayed in order based on the order of the index property.
        ContextMenuItem {
            // The index of the item, used to determine the order in which items are displayed.
            index: 0,
            // The value of the item which will be passed to the on_select callback when the item is selected.
            value: "",
            on_select: |value: String| {
                // This callback is triggered when the item is selected.
                // The value parameter contains the value of the selected item.
            },
        }
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn ContextMenu(props: ContextMenuProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ContextMenuTrigger(props: ContextMenuTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ContextMenuContent(props: ContextMenuContentProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ContextMenuItem(props: ContextMenuItemProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::context_menu::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut selected_item = use_signal(|| None);

    rsx! {
        ContextMenu {
            ContextMenuTrigger { "right click here" }
            ContextMenuContent {
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "edit".to_string(),
                    index: 0usize,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Edit"
                }
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "undo".to_string(),
                    index: 1usize,
                    disabled: true,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Undo"
                }
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "duplicate".to_string(),
                    index: 2usize,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Duplicate"
                }
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "delete".to_string(),
                    index: 3usize,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Delete"
                }
            }
        }

        if let Some(item) = selected_item() {
            span { margin_left: "10px", "Selected: {item}" }
        }
    }
}
```
